recognize_zh: 肉眼可見抹片表面有藍紫色沉積物（B 在推片尾端成團），低倍下紅血球間散布許多深紫色無結構團塊，高倍為無細胞構造、蠟樣淡紫色的細胞外沉澱物及小球狀顆粒（箭頭），即冷凝球蛋白沉積（cryoglobulin deposits）。
features: Grossly visible blue-violet precipitate on the smear, with a dense clump at the edge in panel B
Low power: multiple extracellular aggregates of dark purple amorphous material entrapping red cells
High power: homogeneous, acellular, lilac to violet glassy deposits without nuclei or granules
Small round extracellular globules resembling platelets or cell fragments (arrow)
Rouleaux-like red cell clustering in background; an intact neutrophil for size comparison
describe_en: Gross inspection of the blood smears shows a blue-violet precipitate, forming a discrete clump in one slide. At low power there are numerous extracellular aggregates of dark purple amorphous material entrapping red cells. At higher power the deposits are acellular, homogeneous, and glassy lilac-violet, without nuclear structure or granules, and small spherical globules are also seen free among red cells, where they may be counted as platelets or leukocytes by automated analyzers. Findings are consistent with cryoglobulin precipitates on a cooled blood smear, which in this clinical setting of bone pain should prompt evaluation for plasma cell myeloma with a type I cryoglobulin.

ddx.vs: Platelet clumps show granular individual platelets with visible outlines, whereas cryoglobulin is structureless homogeneous material that dissolves when the sample is warmed to 37 C.
Stain precipitate is refractile dark granular debris lying on top of the smear in all planes and does not entrap red cells or disappear with warming.
Rouleaux are stacked red cells with blue background staining but lack discrete extracellular amorphous deposits.

ddx.dx: Clusters of tumor or plasma cells
ddx.vs: Tumor cell clusters have nuclei and cytoplasmic boundaries, which the acellular cryoglobulin deposits lack.
